newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called 75 cts to $1 down, Brent steady.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called 75 cts to $1 down, Brent steady.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were called to open 75 cents to $1 a tonne down on Tuesday while Brent was expected to open unchanged to a shade weaker.
August gas oil closed at $160.75 a tonne on Monday, and a weaker opening would take the contract down to key support at $160, brokers said.
"The key on the open will be whether it breaks through support," said one.
August Brent ended more than a quarter of a dollar lower on Monday at $17.82 a barrel. The contract was talked in a wide bid/offer range of $17.73/$17.82 on SIMEX.
Support for Brent was at $17.70 and $17.50 a barrel below that, chartists said.
Brent lost ground on Monday on news of Iraq coming closer to oil sales and on details of timing and volume of upcoming German strategic oil sales, said brokers.
The combination of news pushed the market 50 cents lower, but the sale of 2.8 million barrels of German crude was not as bearish as originally thought, due to the quality of the crude.
"Yesterday it had all day to collapse but it didn't," said one broker.
The German Economics Ministry said the crude will be typically composed of 50 percent Iranian Heavy, 25 percent Arabian Light and 25 percent Iraqi Kirkuk.

U.N. coordinator in Baghdad, Staffan De Mistura, said on Monday that discussions about the Iraqi aid plan had been completed and that the plan will be submitted to the U.N. Secretary-General for final approval by next Monday.
Iraq needed to complete an aid distribution plan before resuming oil sales under a deal with the U.N. that enables Iraq to sell $2 billion over six months.
